prerequisites: Basic knowledge of organizational structure in companies and management structures.
Basic knowledge of processes in production areas.

learning_outcomes.text: Students differentiate between various organizational forms in production companies and categorize the IT systems used there. They name bill of material forms, demonstrate the relationship to work plans, and explain numbering systems used therein.

Students also name methods for job evaluation, factory planning, and modeling of production processes. They differentiate between production planning and production control and assign possible planning tools. Students also explain selected methods for production optimization.
After completing the module, students discuss the advantages and disadvantages of production organizational forms.
They relate bills of materials and work plans to each other and justify the use of suitable numbering systems in the production environment.
In the context of factory planning, students discuss the methodological approach and illustrate the workflows behind it.
Furthermore, they distinguish methods and tools for production planning and production control from each other and illustrate optimization methods for existing production areas.
After completing the module, students evaluate necessary methods and tools for production organization.
They independently carry out factory planning, organize numbering systems within production, and design the processes for successful production planning and control.
They analyze optimization potentials in operational production and use optimization methods for improvement.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals and relationships: Organizational forms in production
Operational information processing: Application systems in the production area, numbering systems, bills of materials, work plans, work plan creation
Work system design: Degree of automation, accident prevention, hazard assessment, job evaluation

Factory planning (from an organizational perspective): Methods and tools, planning phases, representative formation, site planning, degree of cooperation, area determination (of production areas), simulation use
Production process modeling: Funnel model and throughput diagram, production characteristic curves
Production planning and control: Principles, material requirements planning, forecasting models, in-house production control, external procurement control, order initiation, order monitoring
Production optimization: Value stream analysis and value stream design, SMED method
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a written exam. The ungraded assessment is experimental work, which involves completing 2 to 4 experimental tasks.
